rules: One record per decision family. Each record validates independently: a change may only move an ADR to superseded if an ADR inside the SAME family replaces it.
An ADR records the decision and the alternatives it discarded. Rationale lives in the ADR, never in a family manifest.
If an externally-owned file or service changes, the consumer ADR goes to needs-review. That is a consumer-side concern and does not invalidate the producer's decision record.
No control references itself. A risk points at the ADR that controls it; an ADR points at the risk it retires.

Report persistence, escalation and the honesty of the claim

notes: The 'realtime' family is the only one without a controlling ADR: its blockers (stop coordinates, trip identity, position feed) are still open. No component may claim live ETA until that family reaches 'current'.
An ADR may appear in more than one family when it is load-bearing for both. Family state is computed from its own ADRs only.
